What this means for your business

That narrower promise is useful. Write down the questions staff answer every day, put the stable answers online, and test what happens after the visitor chooses an action.

What to watch

  • Hours, prices, policies, or services staff keep correcting.
  • A form that sends nowhere or asks for too much.
  • Booking and payment links hidden behind design flourishes.
  • Nobody assigned to review the site after business changes.

Do this next

  1. Collect the ten questions staff answer most.
  2. Answer the stable ones in plain text.
  3. Give each answer one useful next action.
  4. Review the path monthly and after every operational change.

When Little Fight fits

We connect the website to the real business path and keep it cared for. It should reduce avoidable questions, not pretend to replace human judgment.

Get a plain-English second opinion

insight.answer: Your website is not an employee. It cannot notice, improvise, or care. It can reliably answer known questions and route a customer to call, book, order, pay, or visit.
